title: The Lumen Circle
teaches: Defining the structure of a lumen clock with 7 marks.
visual: A circle appears with 7 evenly spaced tick marks labeled 0 through 6. The numbers are placed clockwise starting from the top (12 o'clock position). A hand points to mark 0 initially.
narration: Welcome to the Lumen clock, a unique timekeeping device based on modulo 7 arithmetic. It features exactly seven marks, numbered 0 to 6, arranged in a circle.

title: The Two-Mark Rule
teaches: Explaining the movement rule: one tick = +2 marks.
visual: An animated hand starts at mark 0. It jumps forward two positions to mark 2, then another two to mark 4. Arrows indicate the direction of movement. The text '+2' appears briefly above each jump.
narration: In a lumen clock, one tick advances the hand by exactly two marks. This means we skip every other number as we move clockwise around the circle.

title: The Full Cycle
teaches: Showing that 7 ticks return the hand to start and visit all marks.
visual: A rapid sequence shows the hand visiting every mark: 0→2→4→6→1→3→5→0. After returning to 0, a checkmark appears next to each visited number to show they were all covered.
narration: After exactly seven ticks, the hand returns to its starting position. Crucially, this process ensures that every single mark from 0 to 6 is visited before the cycle repeats.
